chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father, who said:

I asked him, peace be upon him, about a man whom the salat (prayer) of Maghrib reaches while he is on the road: may he delay it until the twilight disappears? He said: There is no harm in that during travel; but in residence, it should be somewhat less than that. So all of these reports indicate that these times are for those with excuses, because they are restricted by hindrances such as travel, rain, needs, and whatever is of a similar kind; and what further clarifies that...

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the condition in which such delay is permitted
key_terms.الطَّرِيقِ: the road, indicating the state of travel
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: legitimate excuses that justify expanded timing
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence or being settled, contrasted with travel
key_terms.الْحَوَائِجِ: needs or necessities that may affect performance time
key_terms.الْمَوَانِعِ: hindrances or obstacles such as travel and rain
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer under discussion
key_terms.يَغِيبَ الشَّفَقُ: the disappearance of twilight, marking the later time mentioned

ai.seo_question: Can Maghrib salat (prayer) be delayed until after the twilight disappears while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of Maghrib salat (prayer) for a traveler and indicates permissibility in delaying it until the twilight disappears during travel. It also clarifies that such extended time allowances apply to people with valid excuses such as travel, rain, and pressing needs.
